filled.later_source_search_note: never machine-filled; complete machine searches are in _draft.proposals.later_source_search_machine

legend.flags ofr_codification_1989_editorial: a later event or whole-order end read from the OFR 1989 Codification's disposition table (status as of 1989-01-20, OCR cell); whole_end_from_1989_disposition_table marks unqualified revocations offered as whole-order ends under later-events' rule. That table and the later-events OFR catalog notes are the same OFR data, so their agreement is not counted as corroboration by two jobs
legend.gate.errors_if_proposals_accepted: feasibility test only: the suggested candidates and placeholder text were put in a COPY of the claim; whatever still fails there has no machine evidence yet (compact form: clause_*_state x12 means twelve clauses)
legend.gate.errors_now: claim_gate.validate_claim errors of the claim exactly as drafted: the agent's to-do list
legend.gate.only_judgment_left: true when that copy passes the gate: every remaining gap is a judgment the agent makes from evidence already in the draft
legend.gate.placeholder_clause: true when no clause inventory exists: the claim then holds one placeholder clause (DRAFT-PLACEHOLDER-no-clause-inventory) so the gate checks every part (an empty list makes the gate stop early, and the readiness tracker would count the unchecked steps); replace it with the real clauses
legend.later_source_search_partial: machine searches that did not cover the whole corpus (sample runs); their full wording is in SUMMARY.json machine_searches
legend.proposals: candidates already in the claim's field shapes ('proposal'), with 'meta' explaining where each came from; dates are the acting instrument's signing or printed date, never a verified effective date (later-event proposals therefore say date_candidate; rename it to effective_date only after confirming)
legend.proposals.current_predicate[] basis_code: the OFR 1989 Codification prints the order as in force on 1989-01-20 (as amended, editorial text): a lead only; its checked_through is 1989-01-20, so it never satisfies the gate and never counts as a current-law lead
legend.proposals.later_source_search_machine: complete machine searches, never put into the claim: copy the 'entry' of the same search_id from SUMMARY.json machine_searches into claim.later_source_search only after judging it adequate for the order and resolving every CONFLICT line
legend.proposals.original_representation[].acce: false for a compiled transcription (grade compiled_transcription_lead, Richardson): a lead to the official original, never the original by itself; the feasibility test never uses it. official_compilation_* grades are GPO/OFR printings graded like fr-originals (needs_page_check or a medium/low location is never strong)
legend.readiness.by_step: confirm = machine evidence is in the draft or proposals and an agent must check and accept it; agent_judgment = needs reading and a decision; resolve_conflicts = conflicts listed; research = no machine evidence yet; done_now / done_now_by_custody = the tracker already counts it; n/a = not applicable

clause-drafts.what_this_is_not: Draft clause boundaries from saved texts. Not legal conclusions; no status, ledger or count is changed.

basis_code.amending_order_in_status_line: This order is listed as an amendment of another order whose text the U.S. Code ({edition}) prints as current under {where}; its amendment is reflected in that printed text.
basis_code.cfr_appendix_text_reference: An appendix at {where} ({edition}) names or reprints this order.
basis_code.cfr_authority_citation: The authority citation of {where} ({edition}) lists this order as authority for the regulation.
basis_code.cfr_search_excerpt_reference: The eCFR point-in-time search for {date} returns {where} as in force, and its excerpt names this order.
basis_code.cfr_source_citation: The source citation of {where} ({edition}) lists this order as a document that issued or amended the regulation text.
basis_code.cfr_text_reference: Current regulation text at {where} ({edition}) names this order.
basis_code.printed_eo_text: The U.S. Code ({edition}) prints this order's text as a note under {where}, and the note's status line does not say it was revoked or superseded. This is an editorial reprint by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel, not a legal basis by itself; it is a lead that the order was treated as in force when the note was last revised.
basis_code.references_in_text_note: The 'References in Text' note at {where} ({edition}) says statute text there refers to this order.
basis_code.statutory_note_reference: A statutory note (law not classified to a section) at {where} ({edition}) names this order.
basis_code.statutory_text_reference: Statute text at {where} ({edition}) names this order. A statute that relies on, ratifies or incorporates an order can keep it operating; read the section to see how the order is used.

caution.actor_is_amending_order_of_named_order: The note says 'revoked by Ex. Ord. A, as amended by Ex. Ord. B'; B (the later order) is given as the actor.
caution.chronology_impossible: The acting order's number is lower than the subject's: the parse is probably wrong. Excluded from fragments; kept in EVENT_CANDIDATES.csv.
caution.possible_state_local_or_tribal_order: (MENTIONS.csv) Words like Governor, State of, County or Tribe are near the reference.
caution.repeal_wording_check_what_ended: The verb is 'repealed', which the OLRC normally uses for statutes or rules; check that the order itself ended. Kept in later_event_candidates, not in whole_order_end_candidates.
caution.state_plan_approval_part: (MENTIONS.csv) A CFR part approving State plans or programs, where 'Executive Order' usually means a Governor's order.
caution.subject_inside_prepositional_phrase: The order is named inside a phrase such as 'as established by' or 'pursuant to', so the thing that ended is probably a rule, office or statute, not the order. Excluded from fragments; kept in EVENT_CANDIDATES.csv.
caution.text_inserted_by_later_amendment_candida: The revoking text sits inside a printed order that is older than the subject, so a later amendment inserted it; candidates are named in actor_candidate.
caution.text_says_revoked_or_superseded: (MENTIONS.csv) The same text says this order was revoked or superseded, so the mention is not a 'still operating' lead.

currency_code.ecfr_bulk_changed_or_unknown: GovInfo eCFR bulk text; the section changed after 2026-10-14 or its currency is unknown (MENTIONS.csv changed_after_cutoff); verify at the point-in-time URL in MENTIONS.csv human_url.
currency_code.ecfr_bulk_no_change_after_cutoff: GovInfo eCFR bulk text; the eCFR versioner lists no change to this section after 2026-10-14 (title amendment dates in SUMMARY.json ecfr.titles), so the text should equal the cutoff text.
currency_code.ecfr_search_point_in_time: eCFR search API queried with date=2026-10-14: the section was in force on that date; the excerpt is partial.
currency_code.usc_release_point: U.S. Code release point 119-121 is current through Pub. L. 119-121 (2026-10-09); laws enacted after 2026-10-09 and on or before 2026-10-14, if any, are not reflected.

date_basis_code.printed_next_to_acting_instrument: The date printed next to the acting order or law in the note (normally its signing or approval date). It is NOT a verified effective date.

scope_candidate.partial_candidate: The sentence names a section, paragraph or provision, is a bracketed '[Revoked by ...]' insert inside the order's text, or is qualified ('insofar as', 'to the extent'); see scope_hint.
scope_candidate.whole_order_candidate: Nothing in the sentence limits the ending to part of the order. Still check the acting instrument.

fragment_codes.snippets: Snippets are whitespace-normalized excerpts; ' | ' joins a heading to a status line or excerpt. They are not byte-verbatim quotes: quote from the source itself.
